observations: Line 2 encodes str via UTF-8 and otherwise calls len() directly on the argument, so any non-str, non-bytes object (e.g. None, int, bytearray) raises TypeError from len() or encode().
Line 2 uses isinstance(body, str) as the sole branch; bytes and bytearray both fall to len(body), but bytearray is not the declared contract type and is silently accepted.
Line 2 has no explicit exception handling; UnicodeEncodeError from encode('utf-8') on lone surrogates propagates to the caller.
Probe p1 wire_size('한글') exercises the str branch; p2 wire_size(b'AB') exercises the bytes branch; p3 wire_size('') returns 0 via the str branch.
Line 1 declares a single positional parameter with no type annotation, so the str-or-bytes contract is not enforced at the signature level.
Line 2 computes length after encoding, so the returned value is byte count, not character count, matching the stated wire-size contract.
